Marked as routine work for “Add shout(text) helper, export it, and test each rule”: the team tries its lightest AI first and moves up if the checks fail.
Choice made for you: shout always adds exactly one exclamation mark, even if the text already ends with one ("wow!" becomes "WOW!!"). The request says 'followed by one exclamation mark', and removing the user's own punctuation could be surprising.
Choice made for you: Capitals come from JavaScript's standard toUpperCase(), with no locale-specific rules.
Choice made for you: Text made only of spaces (for example " ") is not empty, so it gets the exclamation mark: " !". Only the exact empty string "" returns "".
Choice made for you: Anything that isn't a string throws a TypeError with the message "shout expects a string", including null, undefined, numbers, arrays and String objects created with new String(). This matches how capitalize reports bad input.
Choice made for you: The code follows the existing capitalize.js style: a one-line doc comment, a named ES module export, and no new dependencies.
Choice made for you: The tests go in a new file, src/shout.test.js, which the existing npm test (node --test) picks up automatically, so package.json does not change.
Choice made for you: The README is not changed because the request didn't ask for documentation.
Name the tests and the code must agree on: No UI and no HTTP endpoints. This is a JavaScript library (ES modules, "type": "module").
Name the tests and the code must agree on: Module API:
Name the tests and the code must agree on: File: src/shout.js. Contents: export function shout(text) with a one-line JSDoc comment, matching src/capitalize.js.
Name the tests and the code must agree on: src/index.js must contain both lines: export capitalize from "./capitalize.js"; (existing, unchanged) and export shout from "./shout.js";.
Name the tests and the code must agree on: Behavior:
Name the tests and the code must agree on: If typeof text !== "string", throw new TypeError("shout expects a string").
Name the tests and the code must agree on: If text === "", return "".
Name the tests and the code must agree on: Otherwise return text.toUpperCase() + "!".
Name the tests and the code must agree on: Examples: shout("hello") === "HELLO!"; shout("Hello World") === "HELLO WORLD!"; shout("wow!") === "WOW!!"; shout("") === ""; shout(42) throws TypeError.

Name the tests and the code must agree on: Use assert.equal for return values and assert.throws(fn, TypeError) for errors.
Name the tests and the code must agree on: Run with npm test (node --test), which finds src/**/*.test.js.
